messages:
sam (Acme): Hey team — since ~09:10 PT we're seeing p95/p99 latency spikes and a handful of 504s from the /v1/generate endpoint. Affects our webhooks and causes retries.
priya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Sam. Can you share an example request id or time window? Any auth changes or deploys on your side?
sam (Acme): request id `req_8f7b2c` around 2026-03-17T16:10:45Z. No deploys, just normal traffic. We did rotate API keys yesterday but rotated correctly.
priya (Support): Thanks. Checking platform side now. @ingress-bot can you surface recent admit/admit-drop logs for tenant acme-prod?
ingress-bot: Pulling logs for tenant=acme-prod from 2026-03-17T16:00:00Z to 2026-03-17T16:20:00Z. Found elevated admission rejections and queue length. Sample: `admit_reject tenant=acme-prod reason=concurrency_limit peak=128 limit=100`
elena (SRE): That looks like the tenant hit a concurrency cap and the admission controller started rejecting. p95/p99 go up when rejected requests pile up and retries backpressure workers. Any signs of retry amplification from the client?
sam (Acme): Our SDK retries on 502/504 with exponential backoff up to 5 times. We saw a retry spike right then.
alex (Eng): Two likely contributors: 1) concurrency cap for that tenant (limit=100) + burst of long-running requests (seq len high), 2) auth token rotation might cause some requests to fail-fast then retry. Can you share sample headers for `req_8f7b2c`?
sam (Acme): Here's the sanitized headers we have:```Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED``````x-client-version: acme-sdk/2.3.1````request-duration-ms: 4300```
priya (Support): Duration ~4.3s per request is pretty long — that increases in-flight slots. Elena, can we check host-level queueing? Any workers at >95% slot utilization?
elena (SRE): Yes — worker pool rtx-gpu-12 shows high KV cache churn and long token generation durations for sequences >2048. Utilization peaked ~98% during the window. Admission backlog and retry storm explain p99 spike.
priya (Support): Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) Temporarily raise tenant concurrency limit to 160 for 10m (to drain backlog), 2) enable soft-fail for long tails (serve lower-SLA model variant), 3) ask customer to reduce max retries/backoff or add jitter. Which should we do now?
alex (Eng): I can push a quick increase to concurrency for acme-prod and enable model fallback to a faster 8-bit quantized variant. Will do a 10-minute window and monitor. Also recommend disabling aggressive client retries.
mike (Billing): Quick heads up — increasing concurrency may change metered usage for acme-prod. Priya, please confirm with customer before enabling if they care about immediate cost.
priya (Support): Sam — we can make a temporary change to give you relief while we root cause. It will likely increase token consumption/cost a bit. OK to proceed?
sam (Acme): Go ahead, please. We prefer availability over cost for the next 30m.
priya (Support): Doing two actions now: (1) request concurrency -> 160 for tenant acme-prod (10m), (2) enable fallback variant `redwood-fast-v2-q8` for long tails. I'll post updates.
ingress-bot: action=update_concurrency tenant=acme-prod new_limit=160 duration_m=10 actor=alex status=success ts=4075001258
ingress-bot: action=enable_fallback tenant=acme-prod variant=redwood-fast-v2-q8 actor=alex status=success ts=4075001260
elena (SRE): After change backlog is draining; queue length dropped from ~520 to ~60 over 90s. p95 decreased from ~1.2s to ~420ms and p99 from ~3.8s to ~680ms. No more 504s observed.
priya (Support): Sam, can you confirm client-side behavior is normal now? Any more 504s or webhook retries?
sam (Acme): Confirmed — things look stable now, no 504s in the last 3m. Thanks. We'll also patch our SDK to add jitter and cap retries.
alex (Eng): Postmortem action items: (a) investigate why tenant hit concurrency cap — examine traffic spike source, (b) tune admission controller to prefer shedding non-critical traffic earlier, (c) add per-tenant advisory alerts when steady-state in-flight >80% limit, (d) validate model variant perf for long-sequence tails to avoid quality regressions.
elena (SRE): I'll open an incident doc and schedule a follow-up RFC for admission heuristics. For now we should also audit recent key rotations to ensure no auth-induced failure amplification.
priya (Support): Sam — we'll follow up with a summary and recommended SDK retry settings. Current status: mitigated, monitoring for 30m. Closing customer escalation but will keep thread open for postmortem. :thumbsup:
